page: Microsoft Azure M64-16ms is a specialized memory-optimized virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical Intel Xeon 8280M processor cores running at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. Cache distribution includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 105 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is the primary focal point of this configuration, offering 1,792.0 GB of RAM, which equates to an extreme density of 112.0 GB per vCPU core. In addition to system memory, the instance includes 2,199 GB of local SSD storage, while omitting dedicated GPU hardware and complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations reveal an architecture distinctly prioritized for memory capacity over per-core execution speeds. Single-core processing metrics, including stress-ng single-core (1,038.28), Geekbench single-core (887.0), and single-threaded gzip compression (17.21 GB/sec), sit in the lower percentiles. Multi-core performance scales steadily across threads, posting 10,937.09 in stress-ng and 12,033.41 on the PassMark CPU test. Memory subsystem benchmarks show 609.78 GB/sec cached small-block reads, alongside 75.32 GB/sec uncached large-block reads and 63.53 GB/sec large-block writes. Synthetic operational testing measures 10.8 million Redis SET operations per second and balanced database execution benchmarks.

The primary tradeoff of the M64-16ms lies in its asymmetric compute-to-memory allocation. For organizations operating applications constrained by memory limits rather than compute parallelism, this profile offers high cost efficiency by eliminating the requirement to license and provision unneeded CPU cores simply to access terabyte-scale RAM. Appropriate operational fits include large-scale in-memory databases such as SAP HANA or Redis clusters, relational database buffer pools, large in-memory transactional processing, and memory-bound analytics pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure M64-16ms is an extreme memory-optimized instance tailored for enterprise workloads demanding massive RAM capacity relative to processing capacity. Powered by 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical Intel Xeon 8280M cores clocked at 2.7 GHz, the server delivers 1,792 GB of system memory, yielding 112 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware provisioning also features 2,199 GB of local SSD storage without GPU acceleration. Benchmark profiles indicate restrained single-core performance alongside average multi-core and memory subsystem throughput, with Redis throughput reaching 10.8 million operations per second. The instance presents qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy footprints where provisioning larger CPU core counts is unnecessary. Primary use cases include in-memory databases, enterprise caching tiers, large database buffer caches, and high-footprint transactional systems.
